slides.title: Friendly numbers
slides.text: Some numbers are friendly to work with: 50, 300, 1,000. Rounding swaps a number for the nearest friendly one, so your head can hold it.

slides.title: Look at the next digit
slides.text: To round 347 to the nearest hundred, look at the tens digit. It is 4, so 347 stays closer to 300. If that digit were 5 or more, up it would go.

visual.label: 347 on a number line from 300 to 400, nearer to 300

focus.cue: 347 sits between 300 and 400, just left of halfway.
It is nearer 300, so 347 rounds to 300.

slides.title: Rough first, then round
slides.text: Rough first: 268 is a bit under 300. Round it to the nearest ten, step by step.
steps: the ones digit is 8, so round up

visual.label: 268 on a number line from 260 to 270, two away from 270

focus.cue: The hop to 270 is only 2. The hop back to 260 is 8.

slides.title: Stretch: Any place you like
slides.text: Big numbers can round to any place. Round 12,648 to the nearest thousand: the hundreds digit is 6, so it climbs to 13,000.

visual.label: 12,648 on a number line from 12,000 to 13,000, nearer to 13,000

focus.cue: The hundreds digit is 6, so it climbs to 13,000.

words.means: to swap a number for the nearest friendly one
closest in value, with less distance than any other
a smart rough answer, found on purpose
one of the ten symbols 0 to 9 that build numbers

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Sum Racer. It opens on the Rounding Run track, a track of nothing but rounding questions, and it stays there. Win the race: say each number out loud, rounded, before your kart moves.
slides.alt: Sum Racer on the Rounding Run track: a rounding question on screen, four answers to pick from, the karts just off the start line, lap 1 of 3.
